newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai palm oil producers ask for freer imports.
newsitem.headline: Thai palm oil producers ask for freer imports.

text.p: Thai palm oil refineries urged the government to cut import tariffs on crude palm oil to zero from 10 percent currently, an industry source said on Friday.

Somsak Kositset, head of Thai Palm Oil Refinery Association, told Reuters that the crude palm oil should be tariff-free as the government had already removed import duty on soybean, another major raw material for vegetable oil.
"This is to be for fair to the industry. We have already conveyed our wish to the commerce minister who listened well to our concerns," he said.
Somsak said it was too early to say whether the industry would need to import crude palm oil this year or not.
The commerce ministry in November estimated that palm oil stocks -- crude and processed -- stood at 112,995 tonnes, a 117 percent rise from the year-earlier period.
But Somsak said the level of crude oil had dropped substantially in December.

"In November crude stock was around 80,000 tonnes but in December it dropped to around 50,000-60,000 tonnes. We might not need to import if domestic palm fruit output is good. But you never know. It depends on the weather," he said.
